I'd booked what looked like a perfectly nice, cheap hostel online, decent reviews, a good location on the map, and a confirmation email that seemed completely legitimate at first glance.
I arrived at the address after a long day of travel, dragging my suitcase down a quiet street.
I kept checking the map on my phone every few steps to make sure I hadn't taken a wrong turn.
The address matched exactly.
Except there was no hostel there at all, just a regular apartment building with a locked entrance and absolutely no sign of anything resembling the place I'd booked online.
I double, then triple-checked the address on my confirmation email, standing right in front of the building.
I was half convinced I'd somehow read the numbers wrong, despite staring directly at them for a solid minute.
I called the number listed on the booking site.
It just rang and rang before eventually going to a full voicemail box that apparently hadn't been checked in a very long time, the recording itself sounding oddly outdated.
I stood there for a solid ten minutes, suitcase beside me, refreshing the booking app repeatedly.
I was half hoping the address would somehow rearrange itself into an actual building if I just looked hard enough.
A woman walking her dog stopped, noticing my obvious confusion, and asked if I needed help.
Once I explained the situation, she just laughed and said that hostel had apparently closed down almost a year ago.
She mentioned it had actually gotten some local news coverage at the time.
I apparently wasn't the first traveler to show up at that exact address confused, and honestly, that made me feel slightly less foolish.
With no working phone signal to spare and no backup booking, I ended up walking into a nearby actual hotel, exhausted, and asking if they had literally any room left for the night.
They did, thankfully, though it cost considerably more than the hostel I'd booked.
I spent a good chunk of that evening on hold with the booking site, trying to get my money back for a place that plainly didn't exist.
I eventually got refunded, after a lot of back and forth.
Now I always check for a very recent review, ideally from that same week, before trusting any booking site with my actual arrival plans again.

I also started calling ahead now, just to confirm a place actually still exists, which feels like a slightly excessive extra step, but after that evening, it seems more than worth the extra phone call.
